GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx and the CVE both describe CWE-434: FileRules::ext_in allowed a MIME-derived guessed extension (e.g. gif from GIF bytes / image/gif) while ignoring the client filename, so shell.php could pass ext_in[avatar,gif]. Source-to-sink on v4.7.2 (cdf18e8d3f02dfabf96817cd8ef44d2939a38d70): StrictRules\FileRules::ext_in (system/Validation/StrictRules/FileRules.php) does in_array($file->guessExtension(), $params, true) only; non-strict FileRules extends that class. UploadedFile::guessExtension() returns Mimes::guessExtensionFromType($this->getMimeType(), $this->getClientExtension()); File::getMimeType() uses finfo_file on the temp payload. Constructor stores client originalName as $this->name; move($targetPath) does $name ??= $this->getName(), so $file->move($path) keeps shell.php. Impact is RCE only if an app then stores that name in an executable web path; default app has no such endpoint. Regression tests added in 29299349e7d232e9532767c7cefaed30957309be cover GIF bytes named shell.php.
